declaration.intent: Declare The Last Full Stop as a finished creative work under the Giblet's Forge imprint: a fable of the war between Letters and Numbers, ended by the Period, told as a historian's reconstructed archive from three centuries of disputed testimony.

parameters.form: illustrated fable, framed as a historian's reconstructed archive
structure: Interlude. A Digression, Preserved Despite Itself
standing_conventions: Every testimony carries an explicit corroboration label (uncorroborated, disputed, self-reported, corroborated by n sources) — the historian's own evidentiary apparatus is part of the text, not hidden from the reader.
The historian never resolves a disputed account into a single truth; section VI's three-witness dispute over the Period's arrival is left open by design, not by omission.
Section X (the Scribe's Note) is the sole exception: the one claim every surviving witness agrees on, stated once and not repeated as the book's closing line.
Section X precedes XI so the reader meets the Period's final, tired sighting already knowing the one true thing about her.
The Appendix is framed explicitly as the historian's personal conviction, not scholarship — it does not claim evidentiary status for the lost scrap.

constraints: Do not add a fourth account that resolves section VI's disputed testimony.
Do not restore 'she only asked them to stop' as a repeated closing line across more than its two intended appearances (the Scribe's Note, and the back-cover echo).
Do not reorder X and XI back to their original sequence without re-ratifying the restructure rationale.
Any future edition editing the text must re-pin both document hashes and bump this capsule's suffix version.
